blurb: Curly-coated German-French water retriever in toy to standard sizes
description: The Poodle is a water dog of German or French origin with a thick, curly coat, in sizes from toy to standard, known as active, intelligent and trainable.
answer: The Poodle, Pudel in German and Caniche in French, is a water dog bred to retrieve game from water. Most cynologists place its origin in Germany, while the FCI holds that it is French. It comes in Standard, Medium, Miniature and Toy sizes, from 24 to 62 cm under the FCI standard, and is described as active, intelligent and particularly able to learn from humans.

body: The German name comes from the Low German puddeln, 'to splash', and German art from the 17th century shows dogs of recognizable Poodle type. Larger Poodles retrieved shot waterfowl, while French circuses bred smaller dogs for performing tricks, producing the Miniature; the Toy followed in the early 20th century, and the Medium was the last size recognized.
The Kennel Club recognized the Poodle in 1874 and the American Kennel Club in 1886. It was the AKC's most registered breed from 1960 to 1982 and remains one of the most registered breeds in the FCI.

The FCI standard gives 45 to 62 cm for the Standard, 35 to 45 cm for the Medium, 28 to 35 cm for the Miniature and 24 to 28 cm for the Toy; healthy Standards typically weigh 20 to 32 kg. The thick, curly, harsh coat comes in many colors, though major registries recognize mainly solid colors for showing. Show dogs often wear the Continental clip, while pets are usually clipped evenly; corded coats are now rare.

Poodles are commonly described as highly intelligent, energetic and sociable. Stanley Coren's 1994 book ranked them second of 130 breeds in working and obedience intelligence, and the breed standard treats shyness or sharpness as a serious fault. They excel in obedience and are among the most popular service dog breeds.

Owners can expect to have a Poodle groomed every four to eight weeks. The breed is often called hypoallergenic because the curls trap dander and hair, but researchers have generally not found a difference in allergens between breeds. Poodles are athletic and do well in agility, rally and hunt tests.

Poodles tend to live 10 to 18 years, with smaller varieties living longer; a 2024 UK study found 14 years. Conditions reported in the breed include sebaceous adenitis, Addison's disease, allergic skin disease, ear inflammation, hypothyroidism, Cushing's syndrome and progressive rod-cone degeneration. A genetic bottleneck after the 1960s popularity boom is linked to some of these.

faq.q: Is the Poodle German or French?
faq.a: Most cynologists believe it originated in Germany, but the FCI and a minority of experts consider it French. The German name Pudel means roughly 'splasher'.

faq.q: What sizes do Poodles come in?
faq.a: There are Standard, Medium, Miniature and Toy Poodles, though the Medium is not recognized by every club. Under the FCI standard they range from 24 cm (Toy) to 62 cm (Standard).
They are often described that way because the curly coat traps hair and dander, but research has generally not found a difference in allergen levels between breeds.
Poodles tend to live 10 to 18 years, with smaller varieties living longer. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years.
